candidate.subject: daily intake

qualifiers.condition: National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey 2003–2006
qualifiers.metric: potatoes contributed 5% or more of daily intake

candidate.source_evidence_span: Using NHANES 2003 –2006 data, Freedman and Keast (2011) examined the contribution of potatoes 205 to nutrient intakes among children and adolescents. The results indicated that potatoes contributed 10% of daily intake of dietary fiber, vitamin B6, and potassium and 5% or more of thiamin, niacin, vitamin C, vitamin E, vitamin K, phosphorus, magnesium, and copper.
